changes.description: Downloads are judged on what they cost rather than on how wide the area is: the fixed 6 km envelope is gone, and the byte and feature limits are their own numbers instead of following the isochrone graph limit. The default graph size is 50,000 network nodes, which admits a real town. Each instance's /api/status is read before downloading -- free slots, rate limit, and when the next slot frees -- and a busy service is waited for rather than treated as a failure. Responses are kept on the device and reused for the same query; pressing Download again when a network is already saved fetches a fresh one. The widget shows endpoint status before a download, progress on the button while it runs, which instance served the saved graph, and why a download failed.
Reusable local catchment primitive; see docs/experiments/32-john-snow-primitives.md. Bounded prototype, not an exact notebook replay.

evidence.note: Acquisition only; the graph it produces is checked where it is used. The pacing follows the service's own /api/status rather than a client-side guess, measured against OSMnx's behaviour on 2026-10-19.
